```{python}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import requests
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_histogram, geom_abline, labs, theme_minimal,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "docs" / "models").is_dir() or not (ROOT / "models").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
CACHE = ROOT / "docs" / "models" / ".cache"
CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
qbr_path = CACHE / "qbr_week_level.parquet"
if not qbr_path.exists():
    qbr_path.write_bytes(requests.get(
        "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_espn_qbr/qbr_week_level.parquet",
        timeout=300).content)
qbr = pl.read_parquet(qbr_path)
pbp_path = CACHE / "model_pbp_2025.parquet"
if not pbp_path.exists():
    pbp_path.write_bytes(requests.get(
        "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_model_pbp/model_pbp_2025.parquet",
        timeout=600).content)
pbp = pl.read_parquet(pbp_path)
ros_path = CACHE / "roster_2025.parquet"
if not ros_path.exists():
    ros_path.write_bytes(requests.get(
        "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_rosters/roster_2025.parquet",
        timeout=300).content)
ros = pl.read_parquet(ros_path).select("gsis_id", "headshot_url").unique(subset="gsis_id")

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))
```

The QBR model reconstructs an **ESPN-Total-QBR-style 0–100 quarterback rating**
from EPA components, so a QBR can be produced for any game in the corpus without
an ESPN QBR feed. It is a per-(quarterback, game) regression onto ESPN's
published raw QBR, sitting one layer above the [EP model](ep.md) — its inputs are
EPA aggregates, and EPA is the first difference of EP.

This document is compiled: the target-analysis sections below read ESPN's
published QBR (the `nfl_espn_qbr` release this repo also publishes) and the
per-QB EPA aggregates from the published pbp at render time — quantifying
exactly how much of ESPN's number the EPA components can explain, which is the
quantity the model reconstructs.

## Model features

**6 features**, one row per (quarterback, game). Each EPA component is the
per-game **win-probability-leverage-weighted** mean of that component over the
QB's plays (high-leverage plays weighted up, garbage time weighted down), and EPA
is clamped to protect the regression from blow-up plays (`EPA < −5 → −5`,
fumble → −3.5).

| Feature | Type | What it encodes |
|---|---|---|
| `qbr_epa` | numeric | Total QBR-attributable (clamped, leverage-weighted) EPA — the dominant driver. |
| `pass_epa` | numeric | EPA on dropbacks. |
| `rush_epa` | numeric | EPA on QB rushes. |
| `sack_epa` | numeric | EPA lost on non-fumble sacks. |
| `pen_epa` | numeric | EPA from penalties on the QB's plays. |
| `spread` | numeric | Possession-team pregame spread (garbage-time / leverage context). |

## The model

**Algorithm.** XGBoost regression (`objective=reg:squarederror`). The target is
ESPN's *published raw QBR* for the quarterback-game; the EPA components come from
the [EP model](ep.md), so QBR composes on top of EP/EPA. The leverage weighting
mirrors ESPN's clutch emphasis (plays in 0.1–0.2 / 0.8–0.9 home-WP bands carry
0.9× weight, beyond that 0.6×).

**Evaluation.** As a continuous bounded (0–100) target, QBR is checked by
predicted-vs-ESPN scatter rather than a probability-calibration plot. The
render-time analysis below measures the EPA-explainability ceiling directly.

## The target, and its EPA-explainability

```{python}
season_col = "season" if "season" in qbr.columns else "game_year"
q25 = qbr.filter(pl.col(season_col).cast(pl.Int64) == pl.col(season_col).cast(pl.Int64).max())
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame({
        "check": ["ESPN QBR quarterback-weeks (release)", "latest season rows",
                  "mean QBR (latest season)"],
        "value": [float(qbr.height), float(q25.height),
                  float(q25["qbr_total"].mean()) if "qbr_total" in q25.columns else float("nan")],
    }).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="The published nfl_espn_qbr target — render time")
    .fmt_number(columns="value", decimals=2)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Per-QB-week: ESPN QBR vs simple (unweighted) EPA/play from the published pbp — the correlation is the floor the leverage-weighted model improves on."
qb_wk = (
    pbp.filter(pl.col("qb_epa").is_not_null() & pl.col("passer_player_name").is_not_null())
    .group_by(["passer_player_name", "week"])
    .agg(pl.col("qb_epa").mean().alias("epa_play"), pl.len().alias("plays"))
    .filter(pl.col("plays") >= 15)
)
name_col = next((c for c in ("name_short", "name_display", "player_name", "name") if c in qbr.columns), None)
wk_col = next((c for c in ("game_week", "week", "week_num") if c in qbr.columns), None)
joined = None
if name_col and wk_col and "qbr_total" in qbr.columns:
    espn = q25.select(pl.col(name_col).alias("espn_name"),
                      pl.col(wk_col).cast(pl.Int64).alias("week"), "qbr_total")
    def short(n):
        parts = n.split(" ")
        return (parts[0][0] + "." + parts[-1]) if len(parts) >= 2 else n
    qb2 = qb_wk.with_columns(
        pl.col("passer_player_name").alias("espn_name"))
    joined = qb2.join(espn, on=["espn_name", "week"], how="inner")
if joined is not None and joined.height >= 50:
    r = float(joined.select(pl.corr("epa_play", "qbr_total")).item())
    p = (
        ggplot(joined.to_pandas(), aes("epa_play", "qbr_total"))
        + geom_point(alpha=0.4, color="#2a6f97")
        + labs(x="EPA per play (unweighted, published pbp)", y="ESPN Total QBR",
               title=f"QBR vs raw EPA/play — latest season, {joined.height} QB-weeks (r = {r:.3f})")
        + theme_minimal()
    )
else:
    p = (
        ggplot(qb_wk.to_pandas(), aes("epa_play"))
        + geom_histogram(bins=40, fill="#2a6f97")
        + labs(x="EPA per play (QB-weeks, ≥15 plays)", y="QB-weeks",
               title="EPA/play distribution — join to ESPN QBR unavailable this render")
        + theme_minimal()
    )
p
```

The unweighted EPA/play already explains most of QBR's variance; the model's
leverage weighting, clamping, and component split close much of the remaining
gap. What can never close is ESPN's charting-based credit assignment — inputs
the public feed does not carry.

## Results — 2025 QBR leaders

```{python}
if "qbr_total" in q25.columns and name_col:
    agg = (
        q25.group_by(name_col)
        .agg(pl.col("qbr_total").mean().alias("qbr"), pl.len().alias("games"))
        .filter(pl.col("games") >= 8)
        .sort("qbr", descending=True).head(10)
        .rename({name_col: "quarterback"})
    )
    gt_show(
        GT(agg.to_pandas())
        .tab_header(title="ESPN Total QBR leaders — latest season (min 8 games)",
                    subtitle="the published target the reconstruction is trained on")
        .fmt_number(columns="qbr", decimals=1)
    )
```

## Limitations

QBR is a **bounded 0–100** target, so the model cannot perfectly reproduce ESPN's
proprietary formula (clutch weighting and charting inputs we do not have). Treat
the output as a faithful reconstruction of the **EPA-explainable** part of QBR,
not a byte-exact ESPN replica. It inherits the EP model's drift through the EPA
components.
